lines.text: The writ covered every soul in Greyhollow. Including mine. Including the one lord in Aldmere who had promised never to touch a Measuring Stone again.
If he puts a lens on you properly, in daylight, without smoke, it's over.
Then we don't let him.
We can't stop him. Unless the law does.
The Charter of Aldric. Every noble child in the kingdom has to learn the first page by heart. Nobody ever reads the rest. I had read it twice.
So I read it a third time. All night.
Here. The Fourth Article. No lord of the realm shall be measured, held, or questioned in his person, save by the King's own warrant, under the King's own seal.
The King's seal. Not the Grand Measurer's.
His writ covers my people. It doesn't cover me.
And two pages later, I found something else. Something strange.
Any lord may raise to knighthood any commoner who holds a bridge for the realm.
What does that mean?
I have no idea. Yet.
Magister. With respect, you may not measure me. Not without a royal warrant.
The Fourth Article! Oh, that's wonderful. I haven't heard anyone cite the Fourth Article in thirty years.
You're quite right, of course. My writ covers your people. Not you.
Brother Aldo. Ride south today. Ask His Majesty for a warrant, under his own seal.
Six weeks to the capital and back, I should think. And then, well. Royal warrants do tend to travel with soldiers.
I had bought six weeks. For myself.
In the meantime, I'm sure your people won't mind being measured. Shall we begin tomorrow? Everyone. Starting with the children.
Not for them.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter nineteen, coming soon.
